questions.q: What pattern does every AWS CLI command follow?
options: There is no consistent pattern across AWS CLI commands
aws <service> <command> --<parameter> <value>, e.g. aws ec2 describe-instances
<command> aws <service>, with the service always listed last
aws --service=<name> run <command>, with no parameters allowed
questions.explain: Every call names the service, then the command, then any parameters, like aws s3 ls or aws ec2 describe-instances.

questions.q: Which command lists the objects inside a specific S3 bucket?
options: aws s3 describe-objects
aws s3 list-all
aws ec2 describe-instances --bucket my-bucket
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket
questions.explain: aws s3 ls with a bucket URI lists that bucket's contents; aws s3 ls alone lists all buckets.

questions.q: Which --output value is best suited for a shell script that loops over results line by line?
options: There is no difference between the output formats for scripting
table
json, because scripts can never parse JSON
text
questions.explain: text strips formatting down to simple tab-separated lines, which is easy for a shell loop to read.

questions.q: What does --query do that --output does not?
options: It sets the default output format permanently in ~/.aws/config
It changes which AWS region the command runs against
It applies a JMESPath expression to filter and reshape the raw JSON before --output ever formats it
It is simply another name for --output with identical behavior
questions.explain: --query picks which data comes back; --output decides how the result is displayed. They do two different jobs.

questions.q: Why does a --query expression for aws ec2 describe-instances need Reservations[].Instances[] instead of just Instances[]?
options: Because --query cannot be used on EC2 commands, only on S3 commands
Because EC2 instances are not returned as JSON at all
Because describe-instances returns a list of Reservations, each containing a nested list of Instances
Because Instances[] is simply a typo and never valid JMESPath syntax
questions.explain: describe-instances nests instances two levels deep, inside each reservation, so the query has to flatten both levels.
